why: ebullient (bursting with cheerful energy) is a near-opposite of shy/diffident; could be a defensible answer to the opposite question
extol (praise enthusiastically) is a near-opposite of bemoan; ambiguous on the opposite question
stoically (calmly, without showing emotion) is a near-synonym; ambiguous on the closest-meaning question
compunction (guilt, moral hesitation) is a near-opposite of shameless boldness
venial (minor, easily forgiven wrong) is a near-opposite of grossly wicked; ambiguous on the opposite question
disparagingly overlaps with sneeringly/mockingly; near-synonym on the closest-meaning question
sardonically (bitter, mocking) overlaps with caustically/witheringly; near-synonym on the closest-meaning question
hoodwink (to deceive) is the opposite of disabuse (to free from a false belief); defensible answer to the opposite question
'dissipated' in this sense is rarer than the headword and most learners read it as 'scattered/faded'
'objectionable' is a generic word for anything offensive, not a synonym of invidious
